questions.statement: Which words are sports and games?
questions.context: In a park in Bogotá, children play with a ball, a bicycle and a kite.

options.feedback: Apple, banana and orange are fruits, not sports.
Dog, cat and bird are animals, not sports.
Soccer, cycling and kite are all sports and games.
Book, pen and ruler are school objects, not sports.

questions.explanation: Esta pregunta presenta vocabulario básico de deportes en inglés. También se conecta cada palabra con juegos del parque bogotano.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Medellín, a coach says: "In soccer you kick the ball. In basketball you throw the ball with your hands."

options.text: An instruction that says how to play.
options.feedback: A rule tells players what they can and cannot do in a game.
The winner is the result, not the instruction of the game.
The color describes the ball but does not explain the game.
The ticket price is money to enter, not how to play.

questions.explanation: La palabra rule significa la instrucción que explica cómo jugar. También se comprende con ejemplos del fútbol y el baloncesto.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence.
questions.context: In Tunja, a girl says: "My brother _____ his bicycle every Sunday."

options.feedback: "Ride" is plural and does not agree with the singular brother.
"Rides" agrees with the third person singular brother.
"Riding" needs am, is or are and is not correct alone here.
"Rode" is past tense and every Sunday marks a habit.

questions.explanation: El presente simple con every Sunday usa -s en tercera persona. También se practica con el ciclismo boyacense de cada domingo.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: How do players win points in tejo?
questions.context: In Zipaquirá, students read about tejo: "Players throw a metal disc. They aim at packets with gunpowder. The explosion gives points."

options.feedback: Running is not part of tejo; players throw a disc.
Tejo uses a metal disc, not a ball to kick.
Swimming has nothing to do with the game of tejo.

options.text: They hit the packets and cause an explosion.
options.feedback: The text says the explosion after hitting the packets gives points.

questions.explanation: Leer reglas exige identificar la acción que da puntos en el juego. También se aplica con el tejo, deporte nacional colombiano.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which word means the opposite of win?
questions.context: At school in Pasto, teams wear uniforms: "The red team wins the match. The blue team loses the game."

options.feedback: To play means to take part in a game, not the opposite of win.
To score means to make points, which helps to win.
To lose is the opposite of to win in a match.
To train means to practice, not the opposite of win.

questions.explanation: Los opuestos como win y lose describen resultados de partidos. También se asocian con los equipos del colegio en Pasto.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What can you conclude about the three sports?
questions.context: In Cali, a poster says: "Cycling needs a helmet and a road. Swimming needs a pool and a coach. Soccer needs a ball and a field."

options.text: Each sport needs its own place and equipment.
options.feedback: The poster pairs each sport with a different place and object.

options.text: All three sports need the same ball.
options.feedback: Only soccer needs a ball; cycling and swimming do not.

options.text: All three sports happen in a pool.
options.feedback: Only swimming happens in a pool.

options.text: None of the sports needs equipment.
options.feedback: Each sport lists equipment like helmet, pool or field.

questions.explanation: Analizar carteleras permite asociar cada deporte con su lugar y objeto. También se trabaja la lectura comparativa de tres deportes.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: In Barranquilla, a teacher compares: "She can swim very well" and "She swims very well."

options.text: Both sentences describe a daily habit.
options.feedback: Only the second sentence without can describes a habit.
Only the first sentence with can expresses an ability.

options.text: The first shows an ability, the second shows a habit.
options.feedback: "Can swim" expresses ability while "swims" describes what she does.

options.text: The first shows a habit, the second shows an ability.
options.feedback: The roles are reversed; can marks ability and habit needs no can.

questions.explanation: Can expresa habilidad y el presente simple describe hábitos. También se contrasta con la natación que practican los niños barranquilleros.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which invitation is the best for fifth graders?
questions.context: In Ibagué, two invitations to play appear: one lists safe field, referee and water breaks; the other has a highway, no referee and no water.

options.text: The highway game, because cars watch the match.
options.feedback: Playing on a highway is extremely dangerous for children.

options.text: The field game with referee and water.
options.feedback: A safe field, a referee and water protect the children.

options.text: The game with no water, because thirst is good.
options.feedback: Playing without water in the heat harms the health of children.

options.text: Both invitations are equal for children.
options.feedback: The invitations are very different; only one is safe.

questions.explanation: Evaluar invitaciones implica revisar lugar seguro, árbitro y pausas de agua. También se promueve jugar en canchas con adultos responsables.
questions.subject: ingles
